source_text: ἀμφότερα πλήρη σεμιδάλεως ἀναπεποιημένης ἐν ἐλαίῳ εἰς θυσίαν, θυΐσκην μίαν δέκα χρυσῶν, πλήρη θυμιάματος, μόσχον ἕνα ἐκ βοῶν, κριὸν ἕνα, ἀμνὸν ἕνα ἐνιαύσιον εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα. Καὶ χίμαρον ἐξ αἰγῶν ἕνα περὶ ἁμαρτίας· καὶ εἰς θυσίαν σωτηρίου δαμάλεις δύο, κριοὺς πέντε, τράγους πέντε, ἀμνάδας ἐνιαυσίας πέντε. Τοῦτο δῶρον Ναασσὼν υἱοῦ Ἀμιναδάβ.» Προσεκόμιζον δὲ καὶ καθεξῆς ἄχρι τοῦ δυοκαιδεκάτου, κατά γε τὸν ἴσον τρόπον καὶ ἐν ἀπαραλλάκτοις φιλοτιμίαις, ἐκνεμηθείσης ἑκάστῳ τῆς αὐτῷ συντεταγμένης ἡμέρας ἰδικῶς· διετύπου γὰρ ὧδε Θεός. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ τίς δὴ ἄρα ἐστὶ τῆς οὕτω πολυειδοῦς προσαγωγῆς ὁ λόγος; {ΚΥΡ.} Καρποφορία μὲν οὖν τὸ χρῆμά ἐστιν, ὦ Παλλάδιε, πέπλεκται δὲ, οἶμαι, καὶ λόγος αὐτῇ μυστικὸς εἰς τὸν Ἐμμανουὴλ, καὶ εἰς ἡμᾶς αὐτοὺς ἀνακομίζων τὸ αἴνιγμα· φράσω δὲ ὡς ἂν οἷός τε ὦ πάλιν. Ἀναδεδειγμένης γὰρ ἐν τῷδε τῷ κόσμῳ τῆς ἁγίας, καὶ ἀληθοῦς σκηνῆς, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, πολυειδῶς ἐν αὐτῇ διαπρέπων Χριστὸς καὶ μονονουχὶ παρ' ἡμῶν καὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ὡς ἱερὸν προσάγεται θύμα τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ, λύτρον καὶ ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ἁπάντων ζωῆς, εἷς ὁ πάντων ἀντάξιος. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ γέγονεν ἄνθρωπος ὁ Μονογενὴς ὡς εἷς ἐξ ἡμῶν, ἑαυτὸν προσκεκόμικε τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ, πρωτόλειον ὥσπερ τι καὶ ἀπαρχὴ τῆς ἀνθρώπου φύσεως εὐωδιαζούσης ἐν ἁγιασμῷ, φυσικῶς μὲν καὶ οὐσιωδῶς ἐνυπάρχοντι, καθ' ὃ νοεῖται καὶ ἔστι Θεὸς, εἰσκεκριμένως δὲ αὖ διὰ τὸ ἀνθρώπινον. Εἷς δὲ ὑπάρχων καὶ αὐτὸς, κατὰ πολλοὺς ἐγράφετο τρόπους, ὡς ἔν γε τῇ τῶν ἀρχόντων προσκομιδῇ, ἱερουργεῖται δὲ ὥσπερ καὶ νῦν ὁ Χριστὸς, διὰ τῶν κατὰ καιροὺς ἡγουμένων πολυτρόπως νοούμενος, καὶ διαφόροις ὀνόμασιν ἐκτετιμημένος· καὶ καθ' ἡμέραν προσφορὰ, τὸ ἀνεκλειπὲς οἱονεί πως καὶ ἀκατάληκτον τῆς Χριστοῦ θυσίας ἐν ἡμέρᾳ πάσῃ καὶ τὸ ἐν αὐτῇ καρποφόρον τῶν ἐν πίστει δεδικαιωμένων ὑποδηλοῦντος τοῦ πράγματος. Οὐ γὰρ ἐπιλείψουσιν οἱ προσκυνηταὶ, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ σπάνις ἔσται δωροφορίας· προσκομισθήσεται δὲ πρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ὁ Χριστὸς, μυστικῶς ἱερουργούμενος ἐν ταῖς ἁγίαις σκηναῖς. Αὐτὸς δὲ ἡμῶν καρποφορία πρώτη καὶ ἐξαίρετος· προσκεκόμικε γὰρ ἑαυτὸν εἰς θυσίαν τῷ Πατρὶ, καὶ οὐχ ὑπέρ γε μᾶλλον ἑαυτοῦ, κατὰ τὸν ἀμωμήτως ἔχοντα λόγον, ἀλλ' ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τῶν ὑπὸ ζυγὸν καὶ γραφὴν ἁμαρτίας. Καθ' ὁμοιότητα δὲ τὴν πρὸς αὐτὸν, ἱερὰ θύματα καὶ ἡμεῖς, κόσμῳ μὲν ἀποθνήσκοντες, ὡς νενεκρωμένης τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐν ἡμῖν, ζῶντες δὲ τῷ Θεῷ, τὴν ἐν ἁγιασμῷ καὶ ὁσιότητι ζωήν. Ταυτὶ γὰρ ἡμῖν ὑπεμφαίνειν ἔοικεν ἡ τῶν ἀρχόντων προσαγωγὴ, ἣν καὶ ἀνὰ μέρος ἐκβασανίζοντες τοῖς καθήκουσι λογισμοῖς, ὅπως ἂν ἡμῖν εὖ ἔχοι, βούλει λέγωμεν κατὰ τὸ ἐγχωροῦν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα. {ΚΥΡ.} Προσκεκόμισται μὲν οὖν παρὰ ἑκάστου μόσχος· ἐκνενέμηνται δὲ τοῖς ἱεροῖς ἔργοις τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς, ἓξ οὖσαι τὸν ἀριθμὸν αἱ ἅμαξαι. Εἶτα παρ'
pass_a_gloss: Cyril: [Numbers 7:13-17 continued: both full of fine flour (σεμίδαλις) mixed (ἀναποιέω) in oil for sacrifice (θυσία); one incense-dish (θυΐσκη) of ten golds full of incense (θυμίαμα); one calf (μόσχος) from cattle, one ram (κριός), one yearling (ἐνιαύσιος) lamb (ἀμνός) for whole-burnt-offering (ὁλοκαύτωμα); and one kid (χίμαρος) from goats concerning sin (περὶ ἁμαρτίας); and for sacrifice of salvation (θυσία σωτηρίου) two heifers (δαμάλεις), five rams, five he-goats (τράγοι), five yearling ewe-lambs (ἀμνάδες); this the gift of Nahshon son of Amminadab]. They brought also in order up to the twelfth, in the equal manner and with unvarying (ἀπαράλλακτος) munificences (φιλοτιμίαι), to each having been assigned (ἐκνέμω) the day ordered (συντάσσω) for him particularly; for so God prescribed (διατυπόω). Palladius: And what then is the meaning (λόγος) of the so many-formed (πολυειδής) bringing (προσαγωγή)? Cyril: Fruit-bearing/fruit-offering (καρποφορία) is the thing, Palladius, but woven (πλέκω) into it, I think, also a mystical (μυστικός) account toward Emmanuel and toward ourselves, carrying up (ἀνακομίζω) the riddle (αἴνιγμα); I will tell as I am able again. For the holy and true (ἀληθής) tabernacle having been shown forth (ἀναδείκνυμι) in this world, that is, the Church (Ἐκκλησία), Christ excelling (διαπρέπω) in it in many forms, and all but (μονονουχί) from us and for us, is brought as sacred victim (θῦμα) to God and Father, ransom (λύτρον) and exchange (ἀντάλλαγμα) for the life of all, one equal in worth to all (ἀντάξιος). For since the Only-begotten (Μονογενής) became man as one of us, he brought himself to God and Father, as first-offering (πρωτόλειον) and firstfruits (ἀπαρχή) of human nature being fragrant (εὐωδιάζω) in sanctification (ἁγιασμός), [sanctification] existing in him naturally (φυσικῶς) and essentially (οὐσιωδῶς), according as he is understood and is God, but in an introduced/received manner (εἰσκεκριμένως) because of the human (τὸ ἀνθρώπινον). Being one, he was written/depicted (γράφω) in many ways, as in the offering (προσκομιδή) of the rulers; and Christ is sacrificed (ἱερουργέω) as now also, through those leading (ἡγούμενοι) at the times, understood in many ways and honored with different names; and the daily offering (καθ' ἡμέραν προσφορά), the thing hinting (ὑποδηλόω) the unfailing (ἀνεκλειπής) and as it were unceasing (ἀκατάληκτος) of Christ's sacrifice on every day, and the fruit-bearing in it of those justified (δικαιόω) in faith. For worshippers will not fail, nor will there be scarcity of gift-bearing (δωροφορία); Christ will be brought by us and for us, mystically sacrificed in the holy tabernacles. He is our first and choice (ἐξαίρετος) fruit-offering; for he brought himself as a sacrifice to the Father, not rather for himself, according to the blameless (ἀμωμήτως) account, but for us under the yoke (ζυγός) and indictment (γραφή) of sin. In likeness to him we too sacred victims, dying to the world, sin having been deadened (νεκρόω) in us, living to God the life in sanctification and holiness (ὁσιότης). These things the rulers' bringing seems to suggest (ὑπεμφαίνω), which examining (ἐκβασανίζω) part by part with fitting reasonings, as may be well for us, do you wish we speak as possible? Palladius: Very much. Cyril: A calf was brought by each; the wagons, being six in number, were assigned to the sacred works of the holy tabernacle. Then from... [continues].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; one incense dish of ten gold shekels, full of incense; one calf from the herd, one ram, one yearling lamb for a whole burnt offering; and one male goat for sin; and for a sacrifice of salvation two heifers, five rams, five male goats, five yearling ewe lambs. This was the gift of Nahshon son of Amminadab’ (Numbers 7:13–17). And they brought their gifts in turn, one after another, up to the twelfth, in the same way and with unvarying generosity, each being assigned the day appointed for him in particular (Numbers 7:18–83); for this was how God ordained it.
Palladius: And what then is the meaning of so varied an offering?

Cyril: The thing is an offering of fruit, Palladius; but woven into it, I think, is also a mystical meaning, which refers the riddle to Emmanuel and to ourselves. I will explain it again as well as I can. Now that the holy and true tent (Hebrews 8:2), that is, the Church, has been revealed in this world, Christ, shining out in it in many ways, is offered, one might almost say, by us and on our behalf, as a sacred victim to God the Father, a ransom and exchange for the life of all, the One who is worth as much as all. For since the Only-begotten became man as one of us, he offered himself to God the Father (Ephesians 5:2), as a kind of first offering and firstfruits of human nature, fragrant with holiness: a holiness that is his by nature and in essence, inasmuch as he is understood to be God and is God, but that is his in turn as something received, because of his humanity. And though he is one, he was depicted in many ways, as in the offering of the leaders; and so too, even now, Christ is offered in sacrifice through those who serve as leaders in each age, being understood in many ways and honored with various names. The offering each day suggests, in a way, that the sacrifice of Christ never fails and never ceases on any day, and that those who have been justified by faith bear fruit in it. For worshippers will not fail, nor will there be any lack of gifts. Christ will be offered by us and on our behalf, mystically sacrificed in the holy tents. He himself is our first and choicest offering of fruit; for he offered himself as a sacrifice to the Father, not for himself, indeed, as irreproachable reasoning holds, but rather for us who were under the yoke and indictment of sin. And in likeness to him we too are sacred victims, dying to the world, since sin has been put to death in us, and living to God (Romans 6:11) the life of holiness and godliness. This, it seems, is what the leaders’ offering hints at for us. Would you like us to examine it part by part with fitting reasoning, as best suits us, and speak of it as far as we are able?

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opening completes the Numbers 7:13–17 quotation begun in section 29. θυΐσκη δέκα χρυσῶν rendered 'incense dish of ten gold shekels' (LXX 'of ten [shekels] of gold'). θυσία σωτηρίου kept as 'sacrifice of salvation' (LXX for the peace offering) because Cyril reads it typologically later. δαμάλεις: LXX 'heifers' where the Hebrew has oxen; followed the Greek. Numbers 7:18–83 cited for the summary of the other eleven leaders' gifts. 'The holy and true tent' taken as a clear echo of Hebrews 8:2 (τῆς σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς). 'He offered himself to God the Father ... fragrant' cited to Ephesians 5:2 (offering and sacrifice to God for a fragrant aroma). Uncited possible allusions: 'ransom' (Mark 10:45; Matthew 20:28); 'exchange' (Matthew 16:26); 'firstfruits' (1 Corinthians 15:20); 'offered himself ... without blemish' (Hebrews 9:14), since Cyril's ἀμωμήτως modifies 'account', not Christ; 'sacred victims' (Romans 12:1). εἰσκεκριμένως: holiness is Christ's by nature as God, but 'received' or 'brought in' as man; rendered 'as something received, because of his humanity' to keep the contrast without overstating. 'Those who serve as leaders in each age' (οἱ κατὰ καιροὺς ἡγούμενοι) echoes the leaders of Israel and means the Church's bishops and priests; 'the holy tents' means the churches. ἐν ἁγιασμῷ καὶ ὁσιότητι rendered 'of holiness and godliness'. Final sentence: 'a calf from each' and the six wagons assigned to the tent work refer back to Numbers 7:3–5; it breaks off mid-sentence and continues in section 31. ὥσπερ καὶ νῦν read as 'so too, even now' (then in figure, now in fact), not 'so to speak'. κατὰ τὸν ἀμωμήτως ἔχοντα λόγον rendered 'as irreproachable reasoning holds'.
